request_fields.name: required nonempty string; key_name is a compatibility alias
request_fields.algorithm: ES256 by default; released support ES256, ES384, RS256, EdDSA
request_fields.key_purpose: vc_jwt_issuer by default; one canonical signing purpose
request_fields.service_id: managed default when omitted; only managed-openbao-transit supports creation

lti_constraint: lti_tool_signing requires RS256 and cannot share a reference with any credential-signing purpose
long_name_collision_policy: Names up to 256 bytes remain accepted. When the tenant namespace leaves insufficient room for the complete sanitized name, the key reference includes a stable SHA-256 suffix derived from the complete sanitized name. Distinct long names that share the truncated prefix must not select one KMS key.
reviewed_security_tightening: A deterministic organization namespace is included in every KMS key name before a caller-controlled sanitized name, so same-name requests from different tenants never select the same KMS key.
Only explicit managed OpenBao KMS creation is allowed; private key material never enters Rust response, Redis, Gateway, or UI.
An existing KMS key is accepted only when its current public key matches the requested algorithm; purpose bindings are stored only after KMS success.

The public request rejects key-import fields (private_key, public_key, key_type, hsm_config, vault_config), direct KMS endpoint/token selectors, and cross-tenant organization overrides. The released Python handler ignored those import fields; the old UI API comment claiming upload was not an implemented capability.
A failed KMS operation or public-key verification does not record a purpose binding.
acceptance_cases: distinct long names sharing a truncated prefix remain distinct
response never contains credentials or private key material
